data.content_ref: inline:The target identifies the single cross-city modulator as aridity, arguing the nocturnal gap is larger in arid climates because rural evaporative cooling is acutely limited there. However, in arid climates the rural surroundings are also moisture-limited, so rural evapotranspiration is already negligible; the urban–rural latent heat contrast that drives this argument therefore shrinks rather than widens. Empirically, nocturnal UHI is often most pronounced in humid, vegetated regions (where rural evaporative cooling is strong) and weaker in arid regions, contradicting the target’s proposed single mechanism. The target thus answers the cross-city part of the problem with a mechanism that inverts the observed relationship.
